subject: 25D5D8F955CC436AA7A1B20E51D912F3
introduction: “In this wonderful Dispensation, philanthropic undertakings are for all humanity, without any exception.” ‘Abdu’l-Bahá made universality the test of a religion fit for the age: its charity, its temple, its schools and its love may not be reserved for its own. He served the poor of every community in ‘Akká, told American Bahá’ís to advertise their House of Worship as open to all, and said that whatever is universal is from God and whatever is limited is from man. Isaiah’s “house of prayer for all people”, Peter’s discovery that “God is no respecter of persons”, the sun that rises on good and evil, Sa‘dí and Donne are the same recognition. Paul’s “especially … the household of faith” is the ordinary human rule the readings mean to exceed.
questions: What, concretely, did universality require of the people ‘Abdu’l-Bahá was addressing?
Paul says “especially” those of the household of faith. Is some preference for one’s own unavoidable, and is it wrong?
“Every limited matter is from man.” Is that true of the loyalties you value?
What would it mean for a place of worship to be truly open to everyone?

outside.why: In every dispensation fellowship was commanded, but limited to one’s own. The older law at its widest: the stranger that dwelleth with you shall be unto you as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself.

Philanthropy now is for all humanity without exception. Paul kept a preference: let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith. Is there any “especially” left in the readings?
Stranger and friend alike are seated at His table. He maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.
The poor of all nationalities came. Thou shalt open thine hand wide unto thy brother, to thy poor, and to thy needy.
A Cause in this age must be universal. Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons: but in every nation he that feareth him is accepted with him.
Be kind to all people and loyal to all governments. Seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away.
The universal Shepherd. Other sheep I have, which are not of this fold; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd.
“This is a Universal Temple; announce it so.” Mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people.
A church open to everyone. Neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem.
Particular thoughts, of persons or nations, cause misfortune. Donne: no man is an island, entire of itself; every man is a piece of the continent.
Consider the universal in all degrees. Sa‘dí: the sons of Adam are limbs of each other, having been created of one essence.
Every universal matter is from God, every limited one from man. A disciple of Confucius: all within the four seas will be his brothers.

They expected us to serve their old customs. The Samaritan woman states the rule everyone lived by: the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans. What particular loyalties do people still expect a religion to serve?

shortfall: Eighty further readings apply the same principle to schools, charities, meetings and letters; companions were set to the first sixteen.
